question.text: Ms. Sunita Patil, an SIA empanelled with ICAI SIAB, is drafting a Social Impact Report (SIR) for Pragati Foundation, a listed NPO on NSE-SSE. Which SINGLE item is a MANDATORY component of the SIR under SAS-100 irrespective of whether the approach is qualitative or monetary?

answer.text: A description of the scope of the assessment together with assumptions and limitations underlying the analysis
A computed Social Return on Investment (SROI) ratio expressed to two decimal places
A per-beneficiary cost in INR, benchmarked against the Robin Hood Benefit-Cost Ratio
A BACO (Best Available Charitable Option) comparison drawn from Acumen Fund methodology

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 7.3.2 lists the required components of every SIA report: executive summary, information about the organisation, description of scope, data-collection methods, calculation detail where monetary, impact map / ToC, AND assumptions and limitations underlying the analysis. Scope + assumptions/limitations is universal across qualitative and monetary approaches; SROI, cost-per-beneficiary and BACO are only applicable when a monetisation approach is chosen. The Trap: SROI is tempting because it is the most visible monetary output, but it is only required when the monetisation approach is used. BACO and Robin Hood BCR are examples of specific integrated methodologies, not a mandatory SIR component. Cross-Exam Context: Components of an assurance report are tested in III-A/III-C Compliance (SSE disclosure) and XV Research Analyst (equity research scoping), but the SIA-specific list of SIR components is XXIII-only. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Before accepting an engagement, insist that the SE's engagement letter carve out the scope and the data-availability assumptions in writing. Later, your 'Assumptions and Limitations' paragraph in the SIR will simply mirror that carve-out, avoiding last-minute scope disputes with the SE management.
